This seventh criminal appeal under Section 14-A(1) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 (in short "Act, 1989") has been filed against the order dated 13.01.2022 passed by the Special Judge (Atrocities), District Shivpuri, whereby appellant's application for regular bail has been dismissed.

entities.text: Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Appellant is in custody since 22.12.2021 in connection with Crime No.147/2021, registered at Police Station Karera District Shivpuri (MP) for commission of offence punishable under Sections 376,
294, 506, 450 of IPC and under Sections 3(1)(w)(ii), 3(2)(va), 3(1)
(n) and 3(2)(v) of the Act, 1989.

Appellant's first appeal was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 14.02.2022 passed by this Court in Cr.A. No.1543/2022, while second, third, fourth and fifth appeals filed under Section 14-A(2) of the Act, 1989 were dismissed on merits vide orders dated 02.05.2022, 14.07.2022,
06.09.2022 and 04.11.2022 passed by this Court in Cr.A. Nos.3907/2022, 5947/2022, 7413/2022 and 9575/2022 respectively.

Appellant's sixth appeal was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 30.01.2023 passed by this Court in Cr.A. No.1096/2023 with liberty to file fresh appeal in the week commencing 03.04.2023 if the case before the learned Trial Court is not concluded.

Prosecution case, in brief, is that on 28.02.2021 at about 20:30 hours when prosecutrix was all alone in her house, her neighbour appellant knowing the fact that she is a member of Scheduled Castes / Scheduled Tribes community entered into the house and forcefully committed sexual intercourse with her and abused and insulted her by calling her caste name and threatened to kill her and her children if the report is lodged.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that after rejection of appellant's earlier 6th appeal filed under Section 14-A(2), none of the prosecution witness has been examined.
Appellant is in custody since 22.12.2021.
Prosecutrix was admittedly major married lady aged about 40 years.
FIR was lodged after about a month without any plausible explanation.

Trial will still take time to conclude,
therefore, the appellant is entitled for bail in view of the liberty granted vide order dated 30.01.2023.

Learned Public Prosecutor for the State as well as learned counsel for the complainant have opposed the prayer and submits that appellant's earlier appeals were dismissed on merits and since there is no circumstantial change in the matter and the appellant has criminal antecedents and four other Devendra Yadav @ Kalla vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191451884/
2 criminal cases have been registered against him, therefore, he is not entitled for bail.

entities.text: Devendra Yadav @ Kalla vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Having considered the rival submissions, material pointed out by learned counsel for the appellant,
period of custody which is about 1 year and 6 months and also considering the fact that after rejection of appellant's sixth appeal, none of the prosecution witness has been examined, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, this Court is of the view that appellant deserves to be enlarged on bail.
Hence, this appeal is allowed and the order passed by the Special Court is hereby set aside.

It is directed that the appellant be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court with a direction that he will cooperate in trial and present himself regularly before the Trial Court on each and every date fixed by the Court concerned during trial and if during trial, he is found absent without any sufficient cause by the Trial Court, then the bail order passed by this Court shall automatically come to an end without reference to the Court.
With the aforesaid, this appeal stands allowed and disposed of.
Certified copy, as per rules.
(SATYENDRA KUMAR SINGH) JUDGE Abhi Devendra Yadav @ Kalla vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191451884/
